f02.honesty_text: What are the limits of this analysis? Figures rebuilt 2026-09-17 every number re-derived on this date Data checks 153 passed no failures Markets scored 18 of 22 in the network Capture above 100% 13 of 252 measurements Distance travelled Every spend-per-vehicle figure on this page depends on how far the fleet drives. The model applies a single flat 20,000 km a year to every market. The model applies one flat 20,000 km a year to every market. Measured distance tracks truck weight class, a 3.7x spread. Every gap on this page moves with that assumption. Measured annual distance where a sample exists, against the flat model assumption. FleetMeasuredSourceIUK14,494 kmN35 Grafter odometer intervalsUTI51,680 kmCV warranty odometerITUK16,688 kmUK warranty VIN sampleN3512,165 kmCV warranty odometerN7535,217 kmCV warranty odometerF45,630 kmCV warranty odometer Service demand is modelled, not measured 13 of 252 service-family measurements on this page read above 100% captured. That means the assumed demand is too low for those families, not that the market over-performs. The units billed are real billing data. The expected demand they are compared against is a model built from assumed service intervals, pending supplier confirmation. Read the level as directional and the movement as the more reliable signal. How the target spend figure is built Target spend is shown against its ceiling, which is spend per vehicle in service. A second internal benchmark compares spend against an upper reference per market; the two give different percentages for the same market, so each is labelled where it appears and they are never mixed on one figure. Every market is scored on the same approved settings. Those settings, and the list of markets they are applied to, are internal: this tells you what was measured, not how the network's own targets are set. Dealer-level detail Dealer outlet detail exists for some markets and not others. Where it is absent, the national number is shown and labelled
